newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Teltron sees H2 profit rise in tough market.
newsitem.headline: Teltron sees H2 profit rise in tough market.

text.p: South African group Teltron Ltd said on Thursday that it should post a rise in earnings in the second half despite a toughening of its markets.
The firm said high prevailing South African interest rates and consumer debt levels would restrict spending.

"Nevertheless, it is anticipated that the group's headline earnings for the second half will reflect a real increase on those reported for the first half," the firm said in a statement with its first half results.
Earlier the group posted a rise in first half earnings per share to 18.5 cents from 17.5 cents.
The firm has had a troubled recent period after irregularities were discovered in some of its operations, resulting in the dismissal of its previous managing director.
The firm said new managing director Leon Schonknecht was now actively remedying deficiencies in the firm's structure and operations.
Investigations have revealed that various items in the group's accounts have been incorrectly logged leading to an overstatement of past profits.

Teltron said it has not been possible to determine accurately the financial years to which the errors date and amounts totalling 6.7 million rand have been debited from its income statement in the current period as exceptional items.
"The process continues of endeavouring to recover further monies irregularly subverted from the company by other parties acting in concert with the previous managing director," the firm said.
